Subject: Requirements: data residency & retention controls for FinTrust POC

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. For our POC we need clear commitments around data residency, configurable retention, and deletion on request. Our compliance team put together a short checklist (attached) — highlight of asks: 

- Ability to pin storage region per-customer or per-deployment (EU required for a subset of data).
- Per-tenant configurable retention (default 365d but editable) with enforcement at storage layer.
- API-driven deletion + retention audit logs (time of deletion, requestor, KMS key id).
- Proof points for deletion (logs + sample deletion trace) for procurement/security review.
- Clarify how cached KV/preview data is handled and how long ephemeral artifacts persist.

Can you share: feasibility, proposed timeline for an MVP we can include in the SOW, and any temporary contractual language we should use during the POC?

We are aiming to start the POC in mid-March and need an answer for procurement by 10-Mar.

Attachment: FinTrust-Retention-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Sara Morgan

Lauren / team — quick feasibility notes after an architecture pass. Inline answers below the asks.

> Per-customer / per-deployment region pinning (EU only for segmented data)
We can support region pinning by: (a) tagging orgs with a region preference, (b) routing model/embedding storage writes to region-specific buckets, and (c) configuring inference runtime to avoid cross-region cache writes for pinned orgs. Implementation effort: storage routing + IAM per-region + configuration UI. Rough ETA: 4–6 weeks for hosted (basic) to enable region-hinted storage and routing. Full cross-region isolation + SLA guarantees ~10+ weeks.

> Per-tenant retention policy with enforcement and audit trails
Need a retention policy schema (TTL + approve/deny flags), persistence of policy metadata, and a purge worker. Also must ensure KV cache invalidation and any derived artifacts are included. Implementation effort: policy schema + policy evaluation at write/read + purge worker + audit logging. Rough ETA: 6–8 weeks for a basic TTL-enforced pipeline (hosted).

> API-driven deletion + demonstrable deletion evidence
We can surface a deletion API that enqueues a purge job and returns a deletion token. To provide evidence, we need to emit signed audit records (timestamp, object IDs, KMS key info) and a deletion proof package (JSON + signature). KMS integration required for proof integrity. ETA: deliverable depends on KMS work; estimate 8–12 weeks if KMS work is prioritized.

> Cache/KV handling
Caches complicate immediate deletion guarantees. We'll need KV eviction notifications plus a background scrubbing job. Suggest a contract-level note that caches are scrubbed within X hours for POC (X to be defined — recommend 24h).

Major blockers / dependencies:
- KMS & key id propagation across storage + audit logs
- Region capacity and dedicated buckets for clients requesting strict isolation
- Legal review on deletion proof format (may need consult with Security/Legal)

Minimum viable scope for a POC (to hit mid-March):
- Region-hinted storage routing (EU flag) + documented operational caveats
- Per-deployment TTL configuration (UI/API) that triggers purge worker (best-effort within 24–72h for caches)
- Simple deletion API that returns a deletion token and basic logs (no signed proof initially)

I'll assemble a 1–2 page technical design and a rough project plan. Attachment: retention-design-draft.md

— Dev
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
